findings.title: Cutover cannot run unattended: its sudo commands are not in the sudoers rule
findings.description: `cutover_227_tick_backup.py` is documented as "one command" run by `manta` using `sudo` for root steps (docstring and `project-documents/user/runbooks/200-backup-and-restore.md`, "Enrolment is one command"). But `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:11-29` grants `NOPASSWD` only for named `MT_UNITS`, `MT_RUN`, `MT_INSTALL`, `MT_READ`, and `MT_GIT`. Every privileged call this cutover issues is absent: `psql()` runs `sudo -u postgres env ... psql` (line 59), `setup_backup()` runs `sudo .../deploy/setup-backup.sh` (line 65), `conf_sums()` runs `sudo sha256sum` (line 79), step 3 runs `sudo .../scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh`, and step 5 runs `sudo systemctl restart postgresql@17-tick` (not one of the named units). Also, `rclone`/`pg_lsclusters`/`sha256sum` as root need matching rules. Until these are added, the script fails at its first step (or prompts for a password `manta` may not have), so the entire cutover path is unexecutable as shipped. Add a `Cmnd_Alias` for the exact script/argument paths (keeping the least-privilege intent of the existing rule) and a test/guard that parses the alias against the commands `cutover_227_host.py` emits.

findings.title: A stuck weekly run makes the advertised whole-script re-run impossible
findings.description: Recovery is documented as "fix the cause, re-run the whole script" and the same-day skip at lines 175-177 requires **both** `base/<today>` and the arm file to exist. An unarmed weekly run (`cron_weekly_backup.sh`) calls `backup_prod.sh --dest $BASE_DIR/$DATE_STAMP`; `scripts/backup_prod.sh:73-77` refuses when the destination exists and refuses leftovers `$DATE_STAMP.inprogress|verify|failed` (lines 88-95). A normal successful first run leaves `base/<today>` but no arm file until line 187; if any later step fails (e.g. offsite check), the re-run re-invokes weekly, which aborts with "destination already exists", and the cutover never reaches the arm step again. The failure table in the slice design (`project-documents/user/slices/227-slice...md:246`) claims "remove a reported leftover, re-run" — but a completed verified backup is not a leftover. Make the weekly step idempotent by detecting a verified same-day base, or skip/step around `backup_prod.sh` on re-run and create the arm file after verifying the base's presence. Add a regression test for "base exists, arm absent".

findings.title: Destructive offsite reconcile is armed before the offsite verification step
findings.description: `arm.touch()` enables `rclone sync --max-delete` and offsite `base/<date>` purges (`scripts/cron_weekly_backup.sh:164-178`) immediately after the weekly job's "done" line. The cutover's own offsite verification is only `step_offsite` (line 207), three steps later. If `step_offsite` fails (B2 mismatch, credentials, or a stuck push) — or simply if the weekly job was still running when it returned — the tick cluster is left permanently armed with an unverified offsite prefix, contrary to TD7's "armed **after a watched reconcile**" (`project-documents/user/slices/227-slice...md:209-211`; runbook 200: "created by the 227 cutover after its first tick weekly run passed" but also "Nothing creates the file but a person: after watching the first reconcile by hand"). Either arm only after step 11 passes, or leave it to the PM (and have `setup-backup.sh`/`step_production` not treat a missing arm as a cutover failure).

findings.title: Cutover swallows a failed WAL push and production health evidence
findings.description: `run_health`, `step_weekly`, `step_metadata` and `step_offsite` invoke `shell()` (`scripts/cutover_227_host.py:53-57`) and ignore `CompletedProcess.returncode`. `run_health` then reads only the **last** line of `backup-health.log` — a stale line from a prior successful run passes the check even when the just-invoked health command crashed. `step_offsite` ignores a failed `tick_commands()["push"]` and can still report PASS if the subsequent `rclone check` finds nothing new. `step_production` (line 224) reads production's health log with `read_text()` outside any `try`, so a missing/unreadable log raises `FileNotFoundError`; `run_steps` only catches `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError` (line 274), so `main()` never writes the promised failure report. The project's Python rules require explicit handling at a process boundary; here failures are silently converted into false PASS or an unhandled traceback. Check each command's return code, capture a per-run log marker rather than the file's last line, and either catch `OSError`/`Exception` in `run_steps` (as the top-level boundary handler) or convert them to `StepFailed`.

findings.title: `setup-backup.sh --check` writes to disk in rehearsal mode, contradicting "changes nothing"
findings.description: The header promises "`--check` changes nothing" and `test_scratch_root_reports_missing_and_never_applies` asserts `not host["root"].exists()`. But `--check --rehearse <dir>` executes `mkdir -p "$REHEARSE"` unconditionally before the check-mode flag is consulted, so a read-only audit creates a directory. The tests never assert `--rehearse` itself is absent (only `clusters/` and `cron.d` inside it), so this is untested. This matters for the periodic drift audit and for the task file's "live read-only check" runs. Guard the `mkdir` with `[ "$CHECK" -eq 0 ]` (apply mode needs it) and add a test asserting `--check --rehearse` leaves the rehearse path absent.

findings.title: Generated cutover report violates the project's mandatory frontmatter
findings.description: `render_report()` emits `docType`, `slice`, `project`, `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated` but no `status:`. `project-documents/ai-project-guide/file-naming-conventions.md` requires `status: not_started | in_progress | complete | deferred | deprecated` in **all** markdown files' frontmatter ("Universal Required Fields"), and `AGENTS.md` reiterates "All markdown files must include YAML frontmatter as specified in `file-naming-conventions.md`". Every recent note (`2026-10-04-226-proof-archive-check.md`, `2026-10-04-226-proof-drop-proof.md`) carries `status: complete`. `test_failed_step_stops_later_steps_and_report_still_written` only asserts `report.startswith("---\ndocType: notes\n")`, so the omission is untested. Add `status: complete` on PASS and `status: in_progress` (or a matching valid value) on FAIL, plus an assertion.

findings.title: Lifecycle "read-only" check with no timeout can hang the cutover and every drift audit
findings.description: `rclone backend lifecycle ":b2:$BUCKET"` merges stderr into stdout with no `timeout`, no `--retries`, and no `--timeout`/`--contimeout`. The rest of this tier is deliberate about bounds (`sync_wal_offsite.sh` wraps every rclone call in `timeout "${TIMEOUT_MIN}m"`; `WAL_SWITCH_WAIT_S`, `PUSH_TIMEOUT`, statement timeouts). A hung B2 endpoint blocks `setup-backup.sh` step 3 once per cluster, and therefore both the cutover (steps 2, 4, 12) and the periodic `--check` audit, with no output. Also, because stderr is folded into `RULES`, a successful rclone call that logs a warning makes `jq -e 'type == "array"'` fail and the script reports `UNREADABLE` — a false alarm. Wrap the call with `timeout` and rclone's own timeouts, and capture stdout separately from stderr so warnings are logged rather than misparsed.

findings.title: Unused `MAIN`/`TICK` imports and test harness that never exercises `main()`
findings.description: `test_cutover_227.py` imports `MAIN` and `TICK` in `cutover_227_host.py:10` with no use; more importantly, unlike `test_cutover_921.py` (whose autouse `_no_side_effects` fixture patches `cutover_common.subprocess.run` and forbids any real subprocess), this new suite has no such guard. The `rendered` fixture legitimately launches `render_cron.sh`, but nothing prevents a future test from reaching `sudo`, `psql`, or `rclone`. No test exercises `main()` (user check, `cluster(TABLE_PATH, ...)` lookup, report path/`status`), `step_guards`, `step_check`, `step_apply`, `step_metadata`, `step_health_clean`, `step_offsite`, or `step_production`'s failure path — exactly the host-facing steps with the highest blast radius. The 921 suite's established pattern should be replicated here. This also loses the "test-with" coverage guarantee for the most safety-critical slice.

findings.title: Legacy pre-227 fallback paths remain in production wrappers
findings.description: `backup_health_cron.sh:38`, `cron_nightly_metadata.sh:38-40`, and `cron_weekly_backup.sh:58-61` retain defaults (`MT_TIMESCALE_MAINTENANCE_URL`, `MT_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET`, the hardcoded `@192.168.1.144:`→`127.0.0.1` rewrite) for the pre-227 cron file. Task 8.3 (`project-documents/user/tasks/227-tasks...md`, "Remove the pre-227 absent forms") is still unchecked, so this is intentional until after the cutover. Flagging only so it is not forgotten: those fallback values are a second source of truth for host facts that the cluster table now owns, and the hardcoded LAN address is a documented hallucination trap. Track 8.3 as the removal point.

findings.title: `production_changes` hardcodes the replication host instead of reading the table
findings.description: `strip_new_args()` hardcodes `--replication-host 127.0.0.1` and `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py:_NEW_MAIN_ARGS` (line ~697) hardcodes the same value, while `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` defines `17/main`'s replication host as a column. If that column changes, the render changes but the cutover's TD3 "production unchanged" comparison and the render test still strip the old literal and report a false diff. Both the helper and the test should derive the expected token from `BackupCluster.replication_host`. Low impact today (one row), but it violates "one value, one source".
